opennyai_summary.12_November_2024__facts:
The appellants have filed this application under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure to amend the valuation portion of the memorandum of appeal.
Accordingly, the filing section of this Court submitted a report stating that the valuation made in the appeal memorandum and the court fee paid accordingly appeared to be incorrect in the light of the law laid down by a Full Bench of this Court in Balakrishnan Nambiar v. Madhavan and Others [1978 KHC 202].
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Section 51 of the Kerala Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act, 1959 provides that the fee payable on a memorandum of appeal against an order relating to compensation under any Act for the time being in force for the acquisition of property for public purposes shall be computed on the difference between the amount awarded and the amount claimed by the appellant.
It has been laid down by the Full Court in the aforesaid decision that the appellants in such cases are liable to pay court fee on an ad valorem basis on the compensation amount they laid claim to in the appeals, under section 51 of the Kerala Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act.
It seems that the attempt of the appellants is to try whether the payment of a hefty amount of court fee could be avoided by resorting to the amendment as sought for in this application.
Therefore, it is not possible to permit the amendment of the valuation portion of the appeal memorandum as requested in this application since it would amount to getting the stamp of approval of this Court for the method adopted by the appellants for court fee evasion.
opennyai_summary.12_November_2024__decision:
Needless to say that the amendment application cannot be allowed.
In the result, the I.A stands dismissed.
I.A.No.2/2024 is dismissed vide order dated 12.11.2024.
The appellants are directed to remit the requisite court fee payable at this stage, within a period of two weeks.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The Reference was under Section 76 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') for apportionment of the compensation deposited in the Court.
The Reference Court found that the claimants Nos.4 to 6 are entitled for the deposited amount.
It is found that under Section 74 of the Act, the appeal is maintainable only against an award under Section 69, the impugned award was passed under Section 76 of the Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The said prayer of the appellants was strongly opposed by the counsel for the contesting respondents, contending that as per Section 66 of the Kerala Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act, there is no provision to refund the Court Fee when an appeal is rejected.
The learned counsel for the appellant Sri.Beyon.T.Varghese cited the decision of this Court in Thomas and Others v. Dr. Sudha and others 2010 (4) KHC 575, in which it is held that Court Fee is refundable when second appeal is rejected as not maintainable.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
In view of the aforesaid decision of this Court as well as the Punjab & Haryana High Court, I find that the appellant is entitled to get refund of Court Fee, when 2025:KER:37322 LA.APP. NO. 97 OF 2024 the appeal is rejected as not maintainable.
In view of this fact,
this appeal is rejected as not maintainable and the Registry is directed to refund the entire Court Fee paid on this appeal back to the appellants.
